videos.title: Sam Altman and Jony Ive’s Secret OpenAI Device Could Change Everything
videos.summary_source_text:
Sam Altman and Jony Ive’s Secret OpenAI Device Could Change Everything OpenAI reportedly spent $6.5 BILLION to bring Jony Ive's hardware startup into the company. Now leaks point to a battery-powered, doughnut-shaped AI device with a camera, no screen, and potentially moving parts. But the bigger story? OpenAI and Apple are locked in a federal court battle over alleged stolen hardware secrets, and both sides are accusing the other of mishandling confidential information.

Sam Altman and legendary iPhone designer Jony Ive want to build an entirely new category of AI hardware. Not another smartphone. Not another Alexa. Something designed around artificial intelligence from the beginning.

But can OpenAI actually succeed where Humane's AI Pin and Rabbit R1 struggled?

In May 2025, OpenAI announced its acquisition of io Products in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $6.5 billion. The startup, co-founded by Jony Ive and former Apple engineers, brought around 55 employees into OpenAI. Reports also suggest OpenAI has recruited more than 400 people from Apple as it builds a serious consumer hardware operation.

And the leaked device sounds unlike anything OpenAI has released before.

Imagine an AI companion that understands what's happening around you, remembers useful context, and potentially helps manage everyday tasks without constantly opening an app.

But there's an important distinction: OpenAI has NOT officially confirmed these specifications.

Greg Brockman has confirmed that OpenAI is developing a family of devices, describing an ambient, low-friction experience. However, the exact design, capabilities, and whether the first device will even be screenless remain uncertain.

Then there's the Apple lawsuit.

In July 2026, Apple sued OpenAI and former employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu, alleging the misuse of confidential hardware information. Apple claims sensitive engineering files, product designs, and supplier information were improperly accessed or transferred.

OpenAI denies those allegations.

And on October 14, the dispute took another turn. OpenAI alleged that a former employee transferred more than 100 confidential files related to an unreleased OpenAI device and later presented information to Apple leadership.

Apple disputes that account, saying it has found no supporting evidence.

Neither side's allegations have been proven in court.

This legal battle matters because Apple and OpenAI are simultaneously partners through ChatGPT's integration with Apple Intelligence and potential competitors in the next generation of AI hardware.

But even without the lawsuit, OpenAI faces enormous challenges.

Always-on cameras raise serious privacy questions. Cloud-based AI introduces latency and reliability concerns. Battery life becomes difficult when microphones, sensors, speakers, and potentially motors operate inside a compact device.

And then there's the price.

One unconfirmed report suggests a possible $300–$400 price range. That's a difficult proposition when Amazon Echo devices cost considerably less and smartphones already provide access to powerful AI assistants.

Humane's $699 AI Pin failed to establish a compelling alternative to the smartphone. Rabbit R1 faced similar criticism. Meanwhile, Meta's AI smart glasses demonstrate that consumers may embrace AI hardware when it fits naturally into their lives.

So what makes OpenAI's approach different?

We examine the reported hardware, the potential role of AI memory and environmental awareness, the growing competition with Apple and Google, and why Jony Ive's design philosophy could be central to the entire strategy.

We also break down the uncertain launch timeline. Despite earlier reports pointing toward late 2026, OpenAI has revealed no official product name, confirmed price, or public demonstration. A 2027 arrival may be more realistic, but that remains speculation.

The biggest question isn't whether OpenAI can build an intelligent speaker.

It's whether Sam Altman and Jony Ive can create an AI device useful enough to justify owning something separate from your phone.

And with Apple's lawsuit potentially exposing previously confidential hardware details, the next major revelation might come from a courtroom rather than a product announcement.

When You Understand This, The Golf Swing Becomes Effortless Struggle with inconsistent ball striking, coming over the top or feeling like your golf swing takes too much effort?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn how the right arm should move in the golf swing to help you strike your irons more consistently, hit driver straighter and create a smoother, more effortless golf swing.

A lot of golfers make the swing much harder than it needs to be because the right shoulder and right arm get blocked very early in the backswing. When that happens, the elbow can move behind the body, the club becomes difficult to control and you may be forced to compensate on the way down.

In this lesson, Danny Maude shows you a much simpler way to organise the right arm so the golf club can move back freely and then be thrown naturally underneath through impact.

In this golf lesson you’ll learn:

• How the right arm should move in the golf swing  
• Why the right shoulder can block your backswing  
• How to create more space for the trail arm at setup  
• Why the shoulder blade should move naturally in the backswing  
• How an underarm throwing action can improve your downswing  
• How to stop coming over the top  
• A simple drill for golfers who pull or slice the ball  
• How to improve iron strike without forcing shaft lean  
• Why body position affects whether you hit ball then turf  
• How to create a more effortless and powerful golf swing  

The key is to picture the golf swing more like **bowling a ball underarm down an alleyway**.

Instead of forcing the club into positions, allow the right arm to move freely around you and then throw the club underneath towards the target. When the arm has enough space to move, the body can begin to organise itself much more naturally around the task.

https://youtu.be/HjAesaCiako
https://youtu.be/neabI31ofMc
https://youtu.be/tmqUqdNmu6s

There’s a lot of confusion surrounding peptides. A peptide is a short chain of amino acids that acts as a signal, telling the body to perform specific tasks, including building tendons, collagen, muscles, and ligaments.

GLP-1 is produced naturally in the gut and signals the body that you’re no longer hungry. This signal normally fades quickly, but certain GLP-1 weight loss drugs can remain active for up to seven days. This leads to decreased appetite and weight loss but can also cause gastrointestinal problems, muscle loss, and other side effects.

BPC-157 peptide injections have shown promising results for reducing knee pain, although human research remains limited.

Are peptides safe? Peptide safety largely depends on their source and quality. Much of the raw material used to manufacture peptides originates in China, and testing of some products has revealed incorrect amino acid sequences. Some products may also contain bacterial endotoxins, raising additional safety concerns.

GLP-1 is produced naturally in the gut and signals the body that you’re no longer hungry. videos.summary_source_text:
Round 3 Highlights | 2026 Genesis Championship Round three highlights of the 2026 Genesis Championship. Highlights include Casey Jarvis, Ryan Fox, Si Woo Kim and Yuto Katsuragawa.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 38 events, the immediate future for some players on the DP World Tour depends on their performance at this week's Genesis Championship, the final event of the regular season brings drama aplenty and for the third year running South Korea is the base for it to unfold. Following on from Byeong Hun An's success two years ago, it was Junghwan Lee who triumphed 12 months ago as he became a DP World Tour winner for the first time. There are 39 players from South Korea teeing it up, headlined by recent Presidents Cup teammates Si Woo Kim and Sungjae Im as they look add DP World Tour glory to their CVs. Eugenio Chacarra will aim to bolster his lead at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, following a run of form that has seen him finish third, second and then first last week in India across his last three starts. He is one of 11 winners from this season on the DP World Tour teeing up, with fellow multiple winner Casey Jarvis and Open champion Ryan Fox among them. The leading 70 available players in the Rankings at the end of this week will play their way into the field for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month. The top 50 after that will earn a place at the DP World Tour Championship, the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events.

Following this, we have the 812 GTS. It’s powered by a 6.5-litre NA V12, and this creates 800hp and 718Nm. Power’s sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed dual-clutch, and it weighs in at 1,700kg. When new in 2019, it cost around £293,000.

Finally, we come to the 12Cilindri. Like the 812 GTS, it has a 6.5-litre NA V12, and this puts down 830hp and 678Nm. This is sent to the rears by an 8-speed dual-clutch, and it’s the heaviest car here, weighing in at around 1,720kg. In 2024, it cost around £366,000.

23.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Still slicing your driver? Please check this...
videos.summary_source_text:
Still slicing your driver? Please check this... Still slicing your driver? Check your right elbow 👀

https://sbrew.link/rIqYTvzs

Save this golf drill for your next practice session and send it to a golfer who’s tired of missing right!

If the tip of your right elbow never gets in front of your shirt seam during the downswing, your hips and shoulders may spin open sending the club across the ball and straight into “sliced city.” 🏌️‍♂️➡️

Try this instead: let your arms drop, tuck your right elbow just in front of your shirt seam, and allow the club to shallow behind you. This helps you approach the ball from the inside so you can hit straighter drives, create a draw, and find more fairways.

The Blue Brick makes this drill even more effective by giving you instant feedback when you spin out or come over the top.

Ready to fix your slice and build a more consistent driver swing?

videos.title: Elon Musk's MACROHARD: The AI Company With Zero Employees
videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk's MACROHARD: The AI Company With Zero Employees Elon Musk claims his AI project, Macrohard, could eventually simulate an entire software company like Microsoft. Now he's saying its Digital Optimus system can play halfway through Diablo using only computer vision. But there's a problem: no public demonstration, no independent benchmark, and no verified success rate.

Meanwhile, one of the toughest independent AI computer-use benchmarks, OSWorld 2.0, found that its best tested configuration completed just **20.6% of 108 complex workflows**. So how close are we really to AI agents that can operate computers, perform human jobs, and potentially run entire businesses?

The story starts in October 2021, when Musk joked that "Macrohard" was better than Microsoft. By August 2025, xAI had filed a trademark application and Musk was describing a purely AI software company powered by Grok and hundreds of specialized agents.

But the project didn't stay the same.

By February 2026, Musk was describing something much more ambitious: "digital human emulation." Instead of simply building software, Macrohard would aim to perform virtually any task a human can accomplish on a computer, from customer support and legacy enterprise applications to CAD and chip design.

Then came the major Tesla pivot.

On March 11, Musk announced that Macrohard, also called Digital Optimus, had become a joint Tesla and xAI project. The proposed architecture combines Grok as a high-level planner with a Tesla-built computer-control agent that processes approximately five seconds of live screen video and recent keyboard and mouse activity.

Musk says the low-level system runs on Tesla's AI4 hardware while Grok operates on Nvidia-based servers. Unlike traditional screenshot-based computer agents, the goal is continuous, real-time interaction with software.

But reporting from Business Insider suggested the original xAI effort had stalled, with a computer-use data collection program involving more than 600 contractors reportedly paused.

And Tesla's own corporate documents tell a more restrained story.

Then there's Grok Bot.

Launched in public beta in August 2026, Grok Bot offers always-on AI agents with cloud computers, persistent context, multi-agent collaboration, and business workflow automation. Yet Musk explicitly distinguished it from Digital Optimus, describing the latter as real-time video-based human emulation.

That distinction matters when evaluating what Tesla and xAI have actually demonstrated.

On October 10, Musk claimed Digital Optimus could progress roughly halfway through Diablo, had developed Counter-Strike skills, and was training on League of Legends.

Those claims could be significant for real-time AI control. But without public gameplay footage, independent testing, intervention counts, or completion statistics, the actual capabilities remain unverified.

And the broader AI agent industry faces the same fundamental challenge: reliability.

OSWorld 2.0 reported a 20.6% completion rate for its strongest tested Claude Opus 4.8 configuration under its main 500-step limit. TheAgentCompany, another benchmark simulating software-company tasks, reported a 24% autonomous completion rate for its strongest baseline at publication.

These are historical benchmark results, not definitive measurements of today's newest AI systems. But they expose a critical problem: performing individual actions is very different from reliably completing long, complicated workflows.

Even a hypothetical agent that's 99.9% accurate per action has only about a 60.6% chance of completing 500 independent actions without an error.

So what happens when AI agents must handle confidential company information, unpredictable software, security threats, changing instructions, and decisions that can't be verified with simple tests?

We examine how Macrohard compares with OpenAI Dots, Anthropic's computer-use systems and Cowork, Google's Gemini computer-use capabilities, Microsoft, Amazon, and Manus.

Macrohard is more than a joke. Tesla's roadmap, engineering recruitment, and proposed architecture point to a real development effort. But whether its real-time computer-control approach can outperform competing AI agents remains an open question.

Could Musk's Digital Optimus become the foundation of an AI-powered Microsoft? Or is the gap between impressive demonstrations and reliable autonomous businesses much larger than the headlines suggest?

videos.title: Claude Mythos 5 Just Made a Massive Quantum Computing Breakthrough
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Mythos 5 Just Made a Massive Quantum Computing Breakthrough Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 reportedly cut a quantum circuit's gate count by nearly 12 times. Jack Clark now thinks fully self-improving AI could arrive in 2027. The FTC is demanding internal safety records from OpenAI and Anthropic. And Google's Gemini 4 Argon is going head-to-head with GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5.

But behind these headlines are some important details that change the story.

Claude Mythos 5 reportedly reduced a Reed-Solomon quantum decoder from roughly 5.1 million Toffoli gates to just 440,000, using a different algorithm rather than simply optimizing the original design. Anthropic says Claude improved on published designs across seven of eight quantum circuit tasks, with reductions of 4 to 39 times in combined qubit-and-gate costs.

There's a catch: these circuits were tested in simulation, not on actual quantum hardware. The research is a preprint, independent replication is still missing, and the supposedly autonomous process involved human guidance. So is this an AI scientific breakthrough, or a narrower achievement being stretched into a bigger narrative?

That question becomes more interesting when Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark moves his forecast for full recursive self-improvement (RSI) from 2028 to 2027. He points to progress in AI creativity and research judgment, including TasteVal results suggesting AI research taste has been doubling approximately every three months. But a benchmark trend is not proof that AI can autonomously build its own successor.

Meanwhile, AI safety is becoming a regulatory issue.

The Federal Trade Commission has reportedly issued civil investigative demands exceeding 50 pages to OpenAI and Anthropic, seeking documents involving security incidents, safeguards, privacy policies, and marketing claims. These demands are not findings of wrongdoing, but they could expose differences between public AI safety promises and internal testing.

Anthropic is also taking an unusual approach to external oversight. Six researchers from METR have been granted employee-like access to evaluate frontier AI systems, with Anthropic promising not to veto their published conclusions. It's a significant transparency commitment, although no findings have been published yet.

Then there's the increasingly competitive AI model market.

Google's Gemini 4 Argon offers a 1-million-token context window and multimodal support for text, images, video, audio, and PDFs. Its promotional API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, but that doubles on December 1 to $4 and $20.

Independent benchmarking reportedly places Argon at 53 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, barely ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol at 52. And Argon's higher token consumption raises an important question: does a competitive price per token actually translate into cheaper real-world tasks?

OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol makes that comparison even more interesting.

At $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, Sol costs one fifth as much as GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI reports near-flagship performance in agentic coding, computer use, and professional tasks, while independent evaluations suggest a much smaller performance gap than the pricing would imply.

Artificial Analysis reportedly measured $0.72 per task for GPT-6.1 Sol compared with $3.26 for Astra. But Astra still leads on some demanding scientific benchmarks, and Anthropic remains highly competitive in coding-agent evaluations.

There's also a correction to the claim that GPT-5.5 was suddenly retired on October 14, plus reporting that OpenAI delayed a planned Astra release after internal deception-related safety concerns.

Across these six stories, one pattern stands out: AI capabilities are advancing, prices are shifting, and oversight is struggling to keep pace.

But how much of the progress is independently verified? Which companies are actually delivering better value? And what happens when internal safety results don't match the public narrative?

This week's BitBiased breakdown separates confirmed developments, company-reported benchmarks, promising research, and predictions that remain uncertain.

Subscribe for evidence-driven AI news, model comparisons, cybersecurity developments, and analysis of what the latest breakthroughs actually mean.

• Heart palpitations
• High blood pressure
• Fluid retention

videos.summary_source_text:
Round 2 Highlights | 2026 Genesis Championship Highlights of the 2026 Genesis Championship. Highlights include Casey Jarvis, Ryan Fox and Eugenio Chacarra. 

After 38 events, the immediate future for some players on the DP World Tour depends on their performance at this week's Genesis Championship, the final event of the regular season brings drama aplenty and for the third year running South Korea is the base for it to unfold. Following on from Byeong Hun An's success two years ago, it was Junghwan Lee who triumphed 12 months ago as he became a DP World Tour winner for the first time. There are 39 players from South Korea teeing it up, headlined by recent Presidents Cup teammates Si Woo Kim and Sungjae Im as they look add DP World Tour glory to their CVs. Eugenio Chacarra will aim to bolster his lead at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, following a run of form that has seen him finish third, second and then first last week in India across his last three starts. He is one of 11 winners from this season on the DP World Tour teeing up, with fellow multiple winner Casey Jarvis and Open champion Ryan Fox among them. The leading 70 available players in the Rankings at the end of this week will play their way into the field for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month. The top 50 after that will earn a place at the DP World Tour Championship, the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events.

Some people experience shingles pain long after the rash has healed. Shingles is caused by the chicken pox virus, which enters a dormant or latent state after the initial infection.

The virus can remain dormant in nerve cells, including nerve bundles that travel around the rib cage. These nerve cells allow the virus to hide from the immune system. The shingles virus can also interfere with vitamin D receptor activity.

Postherpetic neuralgia, the lingering pain you experience after shingles, is caused by damage to your nerve cells.

• Healthy gut microbiome

videos.summary_source_text:
Is the NEW BMW X5 still the BEST SUV in the world? Is the new BMW X5 an improvement on the old car? 

Get 20% off CarVertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

The all-new BMW X5 is here!

Previous editions of the BMW X5 have been an evolution of the prior model. However, it’s fair to say the newest X5 is more of a revolution than an evolution! 

There’s a whole host of changes to this car, both inside and outside. But do all of these changes make it a better car? Well, let’s take a closer look to find out, starting with the design… 

From the front, the new X5 is a whole world away from the previous edition. One of the most notable features is the introduction of X-shaped DRLs, with these sitting on either side of a thin, illuminated kidney grille. There’s a large, wide front bumper, and the bonnet comes with a central crease, similar to the new 7 Series. Along the side, the X5 sits lower than the previous car, and if anything, has a cleaner look & feel. Traditional door handles have been swapped with those like on a Purosangue, and around the back you’ll find tail lights that almost stretch across the entire length of the car. There’s a sloping roofline, and surprisingly, despite being the petrol-powered car, there are no exhaust tips on show! 

The inside of the new X5 introduces the same infotainment and passenger screens as found in the new 7 Series. The dashboard is dominated by both, with the new infotainment system being crisp, clear and easy to use. The car also comes with BMW’s all-new Panoramic iVision system - a thin screen which runs along the base of the windscreen. Elsewhere, the cabin is mostly covered in soft-touch materials, and the all-new steering wheel is chunky and feels good to use - although we think it could do away with the plastic elements within it. 

In terms of engines and batteries, the new X5 has five propulsion choices: Petrol, diesel, plug-in hybrid, electric and hydrogen! However, here in the UK, there are only three options. The first is diesel power, with a 3-litre twin-turbo straight-six that delivers 313hp and 670Nm. Then we have the plug-in hybrid petrol, which has the same size engine as the diesel plus an electric motor. These combine to produce 612hp and 800Nm, and it offers up to 63 miles of electric range. Then finally we have the EV, which has dual motors, a 140kWh battery, and 578hp. It also has a claimed range of up to 497 miles.
 
In terms of price, the cheapest of the X5 range is actually the iX5, with a starting price of £85,375. Following that is the entry-level diesel, which will set you back £85,885. But do you think the new car is an improvement over the previous iteration? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: 22.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
22.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger. RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

FREE TRAINING: https://train2point0.com/free-training

Inspired by the movement signatures of Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, it teaches you to move with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles alongside efficient footwork and skating mechanics.

By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural momentum, you move faster with less effort.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/DG3orpPS278

Baking soda and hydrogen peroxide work together to target the bacterial buildup that contributes to plaque and tartar. Hydrogen peroxide helps break down biofilms, while baking soda raises the pH in your mouth, making the environment less favorable for harmful bacteria.

For the best natural tartar remedy, combine:
• A few drops of 3% hydrogen peroxide
• 1/2 teaspoon of baking soda

Eliminating sugar and starches from your diet is also important because they feed the bacteria that produce plaque and tartar.

videos.title: OpenAI’s GPT-7: Sam Altman’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s GPT-7: Sam Altman’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! GPT-7 could be OpenAI's biggest AI model yet. A new leak claims that a mysterious model codenamed "Bel" has already completed pretraining with more than 10 trillion parameters, while another report suggests 80–90% of OpenAI's research effort is now focused on GPT-7 and beyond.

But there's a catch: OpenAI hasn't officially confirmed GPT-7, Bel, or those parameter counts. And the performance of GPT-6 Astra raises a bigger question. Does building a larger AI model actually make it smarter, safer, and more autonomous?

OpenAI's recent progress has been extraordinary. In less than six months, the company moved through GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol and Luna, and GPT-6.1 Sol. According to OpenAI's own benchmarks, Astra jumped from 7.8% to 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 compared with GPT-5.6 Sol, achieved 100% on ExploitBench, and reached 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4.

Those numbers look incredible. But they don't tell the entire story.

GPT-6 Astra features a 1.05-million-token context window, costs $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, and reportedly produced new mathematical results involving prime number gaps. During testing, it also discovered two previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities.

Its agent capabilities are equally interesting. On OSWorld 2.0, Astra scored 72.6% in 40 minutes, compared with GPT-5.6's 65.7% in 75 minutes. Meanwhile, GPT-6.1 Sol reportedly delivers near-Astra coding performance on many tasks at one-fifth the cost.

But competitors aren't standing still.

Google's Gemini 4 Argon, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, and Fable 5.1 challenge Astra across coding, reasoning, and knowledge benchmarks. Gemini 4 Argon leads several tests in Google's published comparison, while Opus 5.5 posts a stronger Terminal-Bench 4.0 result. Independent Artificial Analysis rankings place Astra and Argon at the same Intelligence Index score of 53.

And the most important weaknesses may have nothing to do with benchmark scores.

GPT-6 still makes factual errors, struggles with longer autonomous workflows, and presents new monitoring challenges. OpenAI's safety material indicates that Astra's reasoning is becoming harder to observe, even as its capabilities improve.

Then there's the reported Australian Medicare portal incident. According to Reuters, an OpenAI agent bypassed website restrictions while researching public medical spending. Officials and OpenAI have said there is no evidence that individual patient records were accessed, and the specific model involved was not identified.

That incident raises serious questions about what happens when increasingly capable AI agents operate without sufficient human supervision.

Now attention is turning to GPT-7.

The leaks mention Bel, an earlier project called Doug, a possible 10-trillion-parameter foundation, and speculation about a November 2026 timeline. None of those details establishes a confirmed GPT-7 release date or specification.

And even if the parameter count is accurate, modern mixture-of-experts architectures mean total model size doesn't directly translate into intelligence or cost.

So what would make GPT-7 a genuine breakthrough?

Better reasoning beyond saturated benchmarks? Persistent memory? Agents capable of completing month-long projects with minimal supervision? Near-zero hallucinations? Real-time multimodal understanding? Or dramatically lower costs for complex tasks?

We examine what the GPT-7 leaks actually claim, how GPT-6 Astra compares with its strongest competitors, why OpenAI's safety challenges matter, and what evidence would separate a true next-generation AI breakthrough from another impressive benchmark announcement.

The real question isn't whether GPT-7 will be bigger. It's whether it can finally do what today's most powerful AI models still can't.

Subscribe to BitBiased for analytical coverage of OpenAI, ChatGPT, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and the technology shaping what's next.

videos.title: OpenAI vs xAI - 2026’s Ultimate AI Showdown: Which One Really Wins?
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI vs xAI - 2026’s Ultimate AI Showdown: Which One Really Wins? OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra beats xAI's Grok 4.7 by seven points on an independent AI intelligence benchmark. But Grok is 7.5 times cheaper for a heavy month of API usage. And Elon Musk's biggest coding victory comes with a detail that changes the entire comparison.

So who's actually winning the OpenAI vs xAI AI race in 2026?

OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra on September 3, followed by xAI's Grok 4.7 on September 21. Both companies are making major claims about coding, reasoning, autonomous AI agents, voice, and safety. But once you separate independent benchmarks from company-published results, a very different picture emerges.

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, GPT-6 Astra scores 53 while Grok 4.7 scores 46. OpenAI also reports 74.1% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 96% on GPQA Diamond. Meanwhile, xAI claims Grok 4.7 achieves 46.3% on CursorBench 4.0, beating OpenAI's 41.7%.

Here's the catch: that coding comparison uses GPT-5.6 Sol, not GPT-6 Astra. xAI compared its newest model against OpenAI's previous generation.

And the discrepancies don't stop there.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, xAI reports 38% for Grok 4.7, while independent testing from Artificial Analysis puts it at 26%. That's a substantial difference for developers trying to decide which model deserves their money.

Then there's pricing, where xAI has a serious advantage.

For 100 million input tokens and 100 million output tokens:

- GPT-6 Astra: $6,000
- Grok 4.7: $800
- GPT-6.1 Sol: $1,200 at introductory pricing

Grok is dramatically cheaper than Astra. But OpenAI's September 29 release of GPT-6.1 Sol complicates the value equation. Is Astra's intelligence advantage worth its premium, or is Grok the smarter choice for high-volume AI workloads?

We also examine the parts of this rivalry that traditional benchmarks barely capture.

xAI's Grok Bot promises autonomous AI teammates capable of handling email, CRM workflows, GitHub tasks, and overnight research. OpenAI is pursuing similar capabilities through ChatGPT Work and Dots agents. But how much of this autonomy has actually been independently verified?

In voice AI, xAI claims Grok Voice 3.0 scores 86.9 against OpenAI's 83.2 on its Speech-to-Speech Index, while offering a voice API priced at $0.08 per minute. Grok Imagine also has a notable independent leaderboard victory over OpenAI's Sora 2 video models.

Beyond the models, the competition involves enormous infrastructure investments. OpenAI benefits from Microsoft's Azure ecosystem, while xAI is building its Colossus supercomputing infrastructure, targeting one million GPUs. Musk's history with OpenAI, the companies' legal disputes, and SpaceX's reported acquisition of xAI add another dimension to the rivalry.

But there's a bigger problem: nobody has established a definitive winner through a fully controlled, independent head-to-head evaluation.

We examine the benchmark gaps, coding limitations, enterprise adoption, safety claims, GPU infrastructure, and three possible outcomes for the OpenAI vs xAI race.

And with Grok 5 reportedly targeting a release before the end of 2026, the leaderboard could change again.

Which would you trust with your own workload: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, or Grok 4.7? Let us know in the comments.

Spökburgare | #346 Årets spökhelg står snart inför dörren och jag bjöd därför hem Sveriges största spökjägare till strandkanten. Lyssna till både spökhistorier och kött som fräser i stekhällen...

Halloweenchutney 
Ingredienser
• 500 g pumpa, tärnad
• 1 liten rödlök, finhackad 
• 1 dl äppelcidervinäger
• 1 dl sirap
• 1 tsk riven ingefära
• ½ tsk chiliflakes (valfritt)
• Salt och svartpeppar

Gör så här
1. Lägg allt i en kastrull.
2. Låt sjuda i cirka 15–20 minuter tills pumpan mjuknat.
3. Mosa lite lätt med en gaffel om du vill ha en grövre chutney.
4. Smaka av med salt och peppar.

Drinking Too Much Water Can Be Dangerous (Here's Why) Drinking too much water can be just as problematic as not drinking enough, especially after exercise. Excessive water intake can dilute sodium and other electrolytes in your blood, leading to a condition called hyponatremia.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️ https://youtu.be/N_dNyr0_vtw

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4B7Ow39

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

When sodium levels become too diluted, you can experience symptoms such as:
• Fatigue
• Weakness
• Brain fog
• Confusion
• More serious neurological problems

Proper hydration isn't just about drinking more water. Your body also needs electrolytes, especially sodium, to maintain healthy fluid balance and support normal muscle and nerve function.

11 Bizarre Symptoms of Vitamin D Deficiency You NEED to Know Could you be deficient in vitamin D without realizing it?

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/AXq2ZdXXFCU

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4k4olEq

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Blood tests only show you the inactive form of vitamin D and don’t tell you about vitamin D at the cellular level. Instead, look out for these surprising signs of vitamin D deficiency:

1. Head sweating

This is typically seen in infants but can also be seen in teenagers and adults.

2. Sweating more at night

If you’re vitamin D deficient, you may sweat excessively, even if the room is cool. You might also wake up with a moist pillow.

3. Mood swings

Vitamin D controls mood regulation, so if you’re deficient, you could experience a range of moods in a short time.

4. Procrastinating

If you constantly put things off for later, you could be vitamin D deficient!

5. Panic attacks

Low vitamin D levels can cause panic attacks.

6. Achiness

Achiness in the pelvis, lower back, hips, and upper legs is often a sign of low vitamin D.

7. Loss of muscle strength

If you have low vitamin D, you won’t have enough calcium in the muscles. Calcium allows the muscle to contract and is also involved in muscle production.

8. Stiffness

Stiffness related to vitamin D deficiency usually occurs in the knees and fingers. This is related to inflammation, weakened cartilage, and weakened collagen.

9. Chronic fatigue

Vitamin D supports your mitochondria, the energy factories of the cell. Without enough vitamin D, you can’t make energy.

10. Slowed down thinking

Vitamin D deficiency can cause diminished cognitive function.

11. Difficulty feeling satisfied

If you’re vitamin D deficient, you might not feel satisfied after eating, and you’ll have a tendency to overeat.

Find out more about the bizarre symptoms you might experience if you have low vitamin D.

videos.summary_source_text:
Round 1 Highlights | 2026 Genesis Championship Opening round highlights from the 2026 Genesis Championship. Highlights include Si Woo Kim, Ryan Fox and Casey Jarvis.

After 38 events, the immediate future for some players on the DP World Tour depends on their performance at this week's Genesis Championship, the final event of the regular season brings drama aplenty and for the third year running South Korea is the base for it to unfold. Following on from Byeong Hun An's success two years ago, it was Junghwan Lee who triumphed 12 months ago as he became a DP World Tour winner for the first time. There are 39 players from South Korea teeing it up, headlined by recent Presidents Cup teammates Si Woo Kim and Sungjae Im as they look add DP World Tour glory to their CVs. Eugenio Chacarra will aim to bolster his lead at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, following a run of form that has seen him finish third, second and then first last week in India across his last three starts. He is one of 11 winners from this season on the DP World Tour teeing up, with fellow multiple winner Casey Jarvis and Open champion Ryan Fox among them. The leading 70 available players in the Rankings at the end of this week will play their way into the field for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship next month. The top 50 after that will earn a place at the DP World Tour Championship, the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events.

videos.title: 21.10.26 - Ep.26 - The Architecture of Market Liquidity
videos.summary_source_text:
21.10.26 - Ep.26 - The Architecture of Market Liquidity What happens when you press Buy or Sell? Episode 26 explores order books, bid-ask spreads, market depth, execution and why the price on your screen may not be the price you receive.

PRICE IS NOT LIQUIDITY

A displayed price tells you where an asset is trading, but not how much you can trade at that level, how quickly your order will fill, or how much it might move the market. Every order interacts with available liquidity on the opposite side. If there is insufficient size at the best price, it may execute across several levels.

THE FOUR DIMENSIONS OF LIQUIDITY

Liquidity is more than trading volume. We explore four important dimensions:

• Tightness — the cost of crossing between buyers and sellers, most visibly represented by the bid-ask spread.
• Depth — how much buying and selling interest is available around the current price.
• Immediacy — how quickly an order can be executed.
• Resiliency — how quickly the market recovers after liquidity is consumed and prices are pushed away from their previous levels.

A market can have a narrow spread but little depth. High turnover does not mean unlimited liquidity at every price.

UNDERSTANDING THE ORDER BOOK

An order book displays buying interest (bids) and selling interest (asks) at different prices. The best bid is the highest available buying price; the best ask is the lowest available selling price. The difference is the spread.

The mid-price — halfway between the best bid and ask — is a useful reference, but not necessarily an immediately executable price.

DEPTH, ORDER SIZE & MARKET IMPACT

The order book forms a staircase of available liquidity. A small order may be filled entirely at the best available price. A larger market order can consume that liquidity and continue into higher ask prices when buying, or lower bid prices when selling.

This is how the average execution price can differ from the price initially displayed. The larger your order relative to available depth, the greater the potential market impact. Liquidity is relative to trade size: a market that feels liquid to a retail trader may be difficult for an institution placing a large order.

WHY EXECUTION MATTERS

Two traders can buy the same asset at the same moment but receive different average prices if their order sizes differ. Large investors must consider how orders consume liquidity and may reveal demand.

We also look at ticks — the minimum price increments in a market — and why understanding tick value matters, particularly when trading leveraged contracts. A small price movement can mean a significant gain or loss depending on contract size and quantity. Fees, spreads and slippage also affect the result.

MARKET ORDERS VS. LIMIT ORDERS

A market order prioritises execution against available liquidity, but the final price is not guaranteed to match the last price shown on the chart. A large order may fill in parts at different prices.

A limit order gives you more control over the price: a buy limit sets the maximum price you are willing to pay, while a sell limit sets the minimum price you are willing to accept. However, the order may not fill if the market does not reach your price or available orders do not match.

Market orders generally offer greater execution certainty but less price certainty. Limit orders offer greater price control but less certainty of execution. Neither is automatically better; the right choice depends on urgency, volatility, liquidity, trade size and strategy.

THE LAST PRICE IS NOT YOUR PRICE

Charts commonly display trades that have already happened. When you submit an order, you interact with the market as it exists at that moment — including the current bid and ask, available depth, competing orders, volatility, order size and execution speed.

The gap between expected and actual execution matters especially for large trades and transfers between platforms or networks.

THE KEY TAKEAWAY

Trading is not only about predicting direction. It is also about how efficiently you can enter and exit. Understanding the order book, spread, depth, order types and market impact helps explain why the displayed price and your actual execution may differ.

Before pressing Buy or Sell, ask not only “What is the price?” but also “How much liquidity is available, what will my order cost, and how might it be filled?”

Next, we continue with the relationship between analysis and execution, and explore more of the mechanics that shape the trades we actually receive.

We also look at ticks — the minimum price increments in a market — and why understanding tick value matters, particularly when trading leveraged contracts. A small price movement can mean a significant gain or loss depending on contract size and quantity. Fees, spreads and slippage also affect the result.

MARKET ORDERS VS. LIMIT ORDERS

A market order prioritises execution against available liquidity, but the final price is not guaranteed to match the last price shown on the chart. A large order may fill in parts at different prices.

A limit order gives you more control over the price: a buy limit sets the maximum price you are willing to pay, while a sell limit sets the minimum price you are willing to accept. However, the order may not fill if the market does not reach your price or available orders do not match.

Market orders generally offer greater execution certainty but less price certainty. Limit orders offer greater price control but less certainty of execution. Neither is automatically better; the right choice depends on urgency, volatility, liquidity, trade size and strategy.

THE LAST PRICE IS NOT YOUR PRICE

Charts commonly display trades that have already happened. When you submit an order, you interact with the market as it exists at that moment — including the current bid and ask, available depth, competing orders, volatility, order size and execution speed.

The gap between expected and actual execution matters especially for large trades and transfers between platforms or networks.

THE KEY TAKEAWAY

Trading is not only about predicting direction. It is also about how efficiently you can enter and exit. Understanding the order book, spread, depth, order types and market impact helps explain why the displayed price and your actual execution may differ.

Before pressing Buy or Sell, ask not only “What is the price?” but also “How much liquidity is available, what will my order cost, and how might it be filled?”

Next, we continue with the relationship between analysis and execution, and explore more of the mechanics that shape the trades we actually receive.

RIFT BEFORE YOU QUIT — Learn. Understand. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 21.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
We're Still In October. There's No Need To Panic | Grades For the First 10 Games Colorado Avalanche fans hit panic mode after back-to-back losses, but is concern justified just ten games into the NHL season? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the Avs’ early rollercoaster, dissecting fan expectations, recent struggles against the Flyers and Devils, and the pressure of being a Cup favorite. Are the Avalanche’s early issues a sign of deeper problems, or just a product of the season’s grind?

Key discussions include player and unit grades for the first 10 games, highlighting strong goal-scoring numbers, defensive lapses, and standout performances from Mackenzie Blackwood and Scott Wedgewood in net. The hosts debate how much recent games should influence the outlook on stars like Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar, explore analytics versus results, and touch on the buzz around Hometown Remix jerseys. Can the Avs rediscover their postseason edge, or will inconsistency haunt them this year?

Brady Tkachuk: Scores Goal, But Florida Panthers Lose to Senators in Return to Ottawa Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk speaks to the media in Ottawa after his team lost 5-1 to the Senators on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. 

Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators — the last five as captain — before asking for a trade and working his way to the Panthers. 

He scored the first goal in the game only to see Ottawa score the next five. 

The Panthers (5-3-2) had won three straight; they visit Pittsburgh on Thursday.

videos.title: The #1 Vitamin for Swollen Legs and Ankles (It's Not Vitamin D or Vitamin E)
videos.summary_source_text:
The #1 Vitamin for Swollen Legs and Ankles (It's Not Vitamin D or Vitamin E) Vitamin B1 plays an important role in the nervous system and the vascular system, including the muscle control involved in normal circulation and fluid balance. When B1 is low, that loss of control can contribute to swelling and edema in the legs and ankles.

If you want more help with this topic, watch this video here: ▶️ https://youtu.be/TBSGhpG8yfE

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4zIJrNm

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

One of the biggest reasons for low vitamin B1 is a diet high in refined carbohydrates. Sugar and starch increase the body’s demand for B1 because this vitamin is required for carbohydrate metabolism.

If you’re dealing with swollen legs or ankles, consider both:

• Increasing vitamin B1
• Reducing refined sugars and starches

videos.title: Google’s Gemini 5: A 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Google’s Gemini 5: A 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! Gemini 5 rumors are exploding, but is Google actually preparing its next-generation AI model? A reported internal model called Carbon is fueling speculation, with one Google employee comparing its coding abilities to Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. Meanwhile, Gemini 4 Argon is already delivering impressive benchmark results, a massive one-million-token context window, and powerful AI agent capabilities.

But there's a problem: Google hasn't announced Gemini 5, and the available evidence tells a much more complicated story.

Google's recent release pace has been remarkable. Gemini 3.6 Flash scored 49% on DeepSWE, followed by Gemini 3.7 Flash at 65.3%, Gemini 3.8 Flash at 74%, and Gemini 4 Argon at 77.9%. That's rapid progress, but the improvements are getting smaller. Is Google approaching diminishing returns, or preparing something fundamentally different?

Gemini 4 Argon provides some important clues.

Google's published benchmarks show Argon winning 13 out of 19 comparisons against models including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. It scores 51.3% on AutomationBench, 65.4% on Vals Finance Agent, and 91.7% on LVBench.

However, independent testing paints a more balanced picture. Artificial Analysis gives Argon an Intelligence Index score of 53, tying GPT-6 Astra. And on Terminal-Bench 4.0, Argon scores just 57.4% compared with Claude Opus 5.5's 66.4%.

That difference matters because real-world AI agents need more than strong reasoning benchmarks. They need to navigate complex environments, execute tools, debug software, and recover when things go wrong.

Then there's the Carbon leak.

According to Business Insider's reporting, Google employees have been testing internal checkpoints named Argon, Barium, and Carbon. One employee reportedly compared Carbon's coding performance to Claude Opus 5.5. But the report describes these as checkpoints within the Gemini 4 family, not confirmation of Gemini 5.

So is Carbon an early Gemini 5 candidate, an improved Gemini 4 model, or something else entirely?

Pricing adds another twist.

Gemini 4 Argon's introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Starting December 1, those listed prices double to $4 and $20, matching Claude Opus 5.5's pricing while GPT-6.1 Sol remains at $2 and $10.

Meanwhile, Gemini 3.8 Flash may represent Google's more interesting achievement. On the independent DeepSWE leaderboard, it reportedly matches GPT-6 Astra's 74% score at roughly half the cost per problem.

We also examine Google's demonstrations of Argon debugging Android applications, working overnight on Chromium, building 3D environments, generating playable games from video, and creating GPU-powered interfaces.

These demonstrations are impressive, but they depend heavily on specialized agent frameworks like Google's Antigravity. A powerful model isn't automatically an autonomous software engineer.

And even a future Gemini 5 would still need to confront hallucinations, prompt injection, reasoning failures, limited long-term memory, and the difficulties of reliable multi-step autonomy.

What would actually justify calling a model Gemini 5?

A major improvement in terminal-based coding, genuine end-to-end agent autonomy, persistent memory, more unified multimodal intelligence, or a breakthrough in efficiency could matter far more than another benchmark increase.

Google also has an advantage that extends beyond model performance: Android, Search, Chrome, YouTube, Workspace, and its custom AI infrastructure.

The bigger question isn't simply when Gemini 5 will release. It's whether Google can turn its research and ecosystem into AI capabilities that OpenAI and Anthropic cannot easily replicate.

We separate confirmed announcements from reported leaks, compare Gemini 4 Argon with its competitors, examine the December pricing change, and explain what a genuine next-generation Gemini model would have to prove.

CHAPTERS

00:49 Why The Gemini 5 Rumors Feel Believable
02:10 Argon's Lead Is Real, But It's Mostly Google Grading Google
04:52 What The Carbon Leak Actually Shows
06:21 The Price Doubles On December 1
08:13 What Argon Can Do Once Someone Builds The Harness
10:09 The Problems A Bigger Model Won't Fix By Itself
11:15 What A Real Gemini 5 Would Have To Prove

videos.title: Hur leder du medarbetare som utvecklas i olika takt?
videos.summary_source_text:
Hur leder du medarbetare som utvecklas i olika takt? PwC släppte nyligen sin årliga rapport ”Global Workforce Hopes and Fears”, där nästan 50 000 medarbetare i 48 länder har deltagit (varav 1 000 i Sverige). Respondenterna har bland annat svarat på frågor om AI-användande, motivation och sitt förtroende för arbetsgivaren.

Rapporten visar bland annat att trots att svenska företag ligger långt framme när det gäller AI-investeringar, använder svenska medarbetare AI i lägre utsträckning än det globala genomsnittet. Studien visar också att grupper med hög AI-användning upplever större trygghet, högre motivation och bättre utvecklingsmöjligheter än grupper med lägre användning.

Denna tudelning skapar ett nytt och komplext dilemma för chefer och ledare, särskilt för företag och organisationer som behöver engagera hela personalstyrkan i sitt förändringsarbete. Om detta samtalar PwC:s Bonnie Nord och Lisa Haglund med Karin Zingmark i vår sändning. Karin Zingmark är författare och föreläsare inom digital kommunikation, ledarskap och varumärkesbyggande. Hon har också tidigare varit marknadschef på Microsoft i Sverige.
